questions.prompt: Define electric current.
questions.answer: The rate of flow of electrical charge.

questions.prompt: State the unit of electric charge.
questions.answer: The coulomb (C).

questions.prompt: State the unit of resistance.
questions.answer: The ohm (Ω).

questions.prompt: State how the current through a component changes when its resistance increases, for the same potential difference across it.
questions.answer: It decreases.

questions.prompt: Define potential difference.
questions.answer: The energy transferred per unit charge as charge moves between two points in a circuit (V = E ÷ Q).

title: Ohmic conductors, filament lamps and diodes

questions.prompt: State how the current through an ohmic conductor relates to the potential difference across it, at constant temperature.
questions.answer: The current is directly proportional to the potential difference.

questions.prompt: State how the resistance of a filament lamp changes as the temperature of its filament increases.
questions.answer: It increases.

questions.prompt: State the direction in which current can flow through a diode.
questions.answer: One direction only; a diode has a very high resistance in the reverse direction.

questions.prompt: State how the resistance of a thermistor changes as its temperature increases.
questions.answer: It decreases.

questions.prompt: State how the resistance of an LDR changes as light intensity increases.
questions.answer: It decreases.

questions.prompt: Give one use of an LDR in a circuit.
questions.answer: E.g. switching lights on automatically when it gets dark.

questions.prompt: State how the current compares at different points in a series circuit.
questions.answer: It is the same everywhere in the circuit.

questions.prompt: State what happens to the total resistance when another resistor is added in series.
questions.answer: It increases (the total resistance is the sum of the individual resistances).

questions.prompt: State how the potential difference of the supply is shared between components in series.
questions.answer: It is shared between the components (the sum of the potential differences equals the supply potential difference).

questions.prompt: Describe the difference between series and parallel circuits.
questions.answer: In a series circuit the components are joined one after another in a single loop; in a parallel circuit the components are joined on separate branches.

questions.prompt: State how the potential difference across components in parallel compares with each other.
questions.answer: It is the same across each component.

questions.prompt: State how the total current in a parallel circuit relates to the currents through the separate branches.
questions.answer: The total current is the sum of the currents through the separate components.

questions.prompt: State what happens to the total resistance when another resistor is added in parallel.
questions.answer: It decreases (the total resistance is less than the smallest individual resistance).

questions.prompt: State the frequency of the UK domestic electricity supply.
questions.answer: 50 Hz.

questions.prompt: State the approximate potential difference of the UK domestic electricity supply.
questions.answer: About 230 V.

questions.prompt: State the difference between direct and alternating potential difference.
questions.answer: Direct potential difference is steady and drives current in one direction; alternating potential difference constantly reverses direction.

questions.prompt: State the colour of the live wire in a mains cable.
questions.answer: Brown.

questions.prompt: State the colour of the earth wire in a mains cable.
questions.answer: Green and yellow stripes.

questions.prompt: State the function of the earth wire.
questions.answer: It is a safety wire that carries current only if there is a fault, stopping the appliance becoming live.

questions.prompt: State the colour of the neutral wire in a mains cable.
questions.answer: Blue.

questions.prompt: State the function of the live wire.
questions.answer: It carries the alternating potential difference from the supply (about 230 V).

questions.prompt: State the function of the neutral wire.
questions.answer: It completes the circuit (it is at, or close to, 0 V).

questions.prompt: State the unit of electrical power.
questions.answer: The watt (W).

questions.prompt: State when work is done in a circuit.
questions.answer: When charge flows through a component that has a potential difference across it.

questions.prompt: State the purpose of a step-up transformer in the National Grid.
questions.answer: It increases the potential difference from the power station for transmission through the cables.

questions.prompt: State the purpose of a step-down transformer in the National Grid.
questions.answer: It decreases the potential difference to a much lower value for domestic use.

questions.prompt: State why the National Grid transmits electricity at a high potential difference.
questions.answer: A high potential difference means a lower current for the same power, so less energy is wasted as heat in the cables.

questions.prompt: Define the National Grid.
questions.answer: A system of cables and transformers linking power stations to consumers.

questions.prompt: State what is transferred between two insulating materials when they are rubbed together to produce static charge.
questions.answer: Electrons.

questions.prompt: State which charge the material that gains electrons is left with.
questions.answer: Negative (the material that loses electrons is left with an equal positive charge).

questions.prompt: State whether two objects carrying the same type of charge attract or repel.
questions.answer: Repel.

questions.prompt: State what a charged object creates around itself.
questions.answer: An electric field.

questions.prompt: State how the strength of an electric field changes with distance from a charged object.
questions.answer: It gets weaker the further away from the charged object.

questions.prompt: State how the force on a second charged object changes as the distance between the two objects decreases.
questions.answer: The force increases.

questions.prompt: Define an electric field.
questions.answer: The region around a charged object in which another charged object experiences a force.
